feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles, with clear domain focus, progressive career growth, and relevant technical breadth. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would improve with tighter structure, less duplication, and more outcome-driven evidence in several bullets.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” profile.  
- Strong credibility: long progression at NACo, large-scale Drupal/web modernization, analytics stack ownership, and public-sector communications leadership all signal depth.  
- Writing quality is generally high: no obvious misspellings, and tone is professional, specific, and aligned to target roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “Topline Skills,” “Core Competencies,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and sharpen focus.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope/activity: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results (growth %, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, cost savings) would increase impact.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation style varies across bullets; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead. Also consider whether “Ranked among the top public universities…” adds value versus more relevant content.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and make the value proposition more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Senior digital leader with 12+ years modernizing public-sector digital platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume communications.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger, more direct verbs such as “modernizing,” “scaling,” or “leading.”
- Consider simplifying the second sentence to group related capabilities: “Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics and editorial infrastructure, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled content experiences.”
- If targeting strategy-heavy roles, add a results cue like “for complex, mission-driven organizations at scale.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Public-sector communications,” “governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” are repeated across Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The subtitle already signals leadership focus, so avoid overloading the intro with another long capability list.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if grouped around distinctive leadership strengths and phrased more consistently.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use tighter, parallel phrasing and emphasize senior-level scope: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting and insight systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Replace broader items with more distinctive ones from recent work: Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia, studio and livestream production
- Consider trimming “Multi-channel communications operations,” which is generic and already well covered elsewhere.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “search and content experiences” vs. “operations”; keep all items as capability areas.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps heavily with the header summary and all three Topline Skills blocks.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” also repeats Technical + IT and multiple experience bullets.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies. It will be stronger if tightened, made more parallel in style, and framed as selected examples rather than restating responsibilities.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Rename to “Selected Recent Projects” and use consistent action-result phrasing for each item.
- Tighten wording and standardize punctuation: e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat.”
- Add specificity where possible without repeating metrics already used elsewhere: note audience, campaign purpose, or platform context.
- Keep each project to one crisp line and use parallel verbs: “Designed,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched/Produced.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance and NACo roles.
- “Built” is repeated three times; vary verbs to avoid a repetitive tone.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list rather than a high-impact recent engagement. Tighten it around 3–4 signature contributions and add outcomes or scale where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards and analytics processes to improve coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-oriented: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components and member toolkits, while providing front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public sites.”
- Keep the AI search bullet, but sharpen it: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content modeling and user-facing discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating NACo-era themes like “governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “large public-facing web properties” unless this role shows a new scale, toolset or measurable result.
- Footer projects already cover the microsite and AI search; keep this entry focused on leadership and business impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in the earlier NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Combine and streamline bullets around channels: replace broad oversight language with one impact-focused bullet on email/social reach only if you can add performance metrics (growth, engagement, CTR, list size, campaign results).
- Make outcomes more explicit: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers.”
- Strengthen operational bullets with results: quantify budget/team size, reporting efficiency, publishing speed, governance adoption, or in-house video cost/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo bullets; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned at this level: newsletters, advocacy video, and cross-team editorial operations.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to clarify scope and level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve alignment and publishing cadence.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency and execution across channels.
- If possible, add metrics: email open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or stakeholder/team count.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid “Led” repeatedly; reserve higher-level leadership language for the Director role.
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership verbs here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and reflect the most recent enterprise/platform leadership angle.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & UX
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with recent roles.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise web strategy for 10,000+ page, 3.5M annual-view platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; vary wording or cut one.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and current strengths rather than listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-signal or dated items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is required for target roles.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” on one line to reduce choppiness.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization and migration for large public-facing sites” to echo recent Drupal leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and project content; mention it once here only if it remains a priority differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and repeats tools already substantiated in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize decision-making impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics, Reporting & Performance Optimization
- Replace the list with outcome-oriented phrasing, e.g.: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity; KPI framework design; executive/leadership reporting; SEO and digital performance analysis
- Put the most strategic items first: KPI framework design and executive reporting before individual tools
- If space allows, add one stronger business-facing term such as “measurement strategy” or “insight generation” instead of “optimization,” which is currently vague

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; consider keeping tools there and making this topline entry more strategic
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics/reporting language; combine or sharpen to avoid filler

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery environment and technical scope rather than broad video terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Studio, Livestream & Hybrid Event Production**
- Tighten content to 4 focused bullets, e.g.:
- Broadcast-style video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- PTZ camera and in-house studio systems
- Virtual event technical direction and show operations
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale/context in adjacent experience bullets instead of here: studio built, recurring programs, live event volume, audience size.
- Use parallel noun phrases; avoid mixing tools, formats, and outcomes in one list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” + “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies wording and NACo experience.
- “Studio operations” overlaps with the Director bullet about building the in-house studio; keep this skills item high-level and let experience carry impact.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section above. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth/relevance or differentiated by adding context such as level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to prioritize strongest/recent platforms: “Drupal (enterprise, Drupal 10) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add proficiency/context instead of a bare list: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; static publishing: GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping the title repetition and renaming to “CMS Platforms” for concision.
- If Drupal is the clear flagship, lead with it and consider a qualifier tied to recent work: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; keep one list shorter or merge them.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, not repeat broader platform skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as applied capabilities: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag implementation • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider replacing “Google Tag Manager” with “Tag management (Google Tag Manager)” for parallel phrasing.
- If accurate, add scope or depth signals: “custom front-end components,” “third-party/API integrations,” or “CI/CD workflows” to show practical use rather than tool familiarity.
- If space allows, order by strongest/current value: JavaScript, API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, then HTML/CSS/jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; either remove them there or make this section more technical/specific.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially overlap with GitHub Actions.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. It will be stronger if grouped by function and trimmed to tools that reinforce recent, higher-value systems work.

Suggested edit:
- Split into clearer categories: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier” and “Work management/collaboration: Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.”
- Cut lower-signal or older/general tools unless they were central recently; Trello and Basecamp are the easiest to drop.
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools” so the collaboration apps feel intentional rather than tacked on.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill set to impact in experience bullets (e.g., automated reporting, intake, approvals, or cross-team publishing workflows).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Slack/Teams may read as generic unless positioned as collaboration tools, not core technical systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools list, but it’s too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership implied by recent email leadership work. Tightening the label and ordering by strongest/recent platform would improve credibility.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely strongest/recent relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just names: **Higher Logic (newsletter/member communications) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation/segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign delivery)**
- Keep it concise; only include platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated “email” references in multiple NACo roles; avoid restating platform names in experience bullets unless tied to a measurable result.
- “Engagement Systems” is broad; don’t imply CRM/marketing automation depth beyond what your work history supports.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a recent, impact-led CV, this section should be tighter and more capability-oriented, with less repetition of tools already proven in the NACo role.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization Tools
- Tighten and group for scanability: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with “KPI dashboarding” or “executive reporting dashboards” to sound more outcome-linked.
- If space allows elsewhere, move proof of impact to experience bullets rather than here (e.g., “expanded analytics infrastructure” / “improved reporting and decision-making”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider keeping one version only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already explicitly referenced in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so avoid repeating the full list multiple times.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs or scale if you can add them.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer scope/results: mention website refresh scale, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, or audience reach if known.
- Tighten the leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” only if it was true managerial oversight.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improve cross-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring livestreams and weekly video updates while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/establishing the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is a useful early-career bridge item, but it reads broadly and undersells the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Tighten it to emphasize initiative, cross-functional coordination, and concrete outputs.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Compress the rest into one impact-oriented line: “Coordinated research and innovation projects supporting county-focused programs, policy initiatives, and organizational communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “Produced multimedia and digital content assets to support program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scale or frequency: number of episodes, audiences served, project count, or types of stakeholders/programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating later multimedia themes already covered in Digital Media Manager / Producer; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and research/program support.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here, since stronger web/video leadership appears in more recent NACo roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize tools, and avoid repeating broader multimedia strengths already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename or sharpen to a true tools list: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep production capabilities, separate them with clearer phrasing: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast editing/production”
- Use consistent specificity: either all brand/tool names or all capability labels; right now “Livestream studio workflows” is less parallel than the Adobe apps.
- Only keep items you’d be comfortable using in a role today; recent, relevant proficiency matters more than legacy exposure.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with “Livestreaming,” “Studio operations,” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” elsewhere.
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older experience; keep it only if still a current selling point.
